title: Letter and Alibi
premise: Isandro Underhill, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent years making themselves unnoticeable, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a murder committed twenty-two years ago, one promising that more will follow unless Isandro decodes the taxi company's old route ledger. The letters come from someone who knows Isandro's real name—the one they buried when they fled their hometown—and each decoded entry pulls them closer to the truth: the murder was committed by the taxi company's founder, and Isandro's own father helped cover it up before disappearing. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Isandro must decide whether exposing the killer is worth surrendering the invisibility that has kept them safe. In the end, Isandro publishes the decoded ledger, confronts the dying founder, and finally claims their own name aloud—choosing belonging over hiding.
about_author: Felix Montrose spent a decade working overnight dispatch jobs in three cities before turning to fiction, writing his first novel on the backs of shift logs. He lives near a harbor he never sees in daylight.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Stamp
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. After a quiet shift dispatching cabs through rain, Isandro finds twin letters in their mailbox—one confessing to a 2003 killing, one promising 'more if you don't look.' Both use Isandro's abandoned birth name. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in a strange, unwelcome thrill at being seen.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Overlooked
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, flashback-tinged. We learn how Isandro built an invisible life: cash rent, no photos, a name shortened to 'Sand' at work. The letters threaten all of it. Beat: the cost of anonymity revealed as both armor and prison.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Searching their late mother's boxes for answers, Isandro finds her old copy of the Meridian Taxi route ledger—her former employer—with odd marginal notations matching the letters' phrasing. Beat: first spark of agency; the hunt begins.

chapters.title: Route 9, Fare 44
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Decoding the ledger's first ciphered entry reveals a pickup address on the night of the murder—a house Isandro recognizes from childhood. Beat: vertigo as the past maps onto the present.

chapters.title: The Founder's Shadow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Augustin Vey, the company's aging founder, in his mansion, burning papers but keeping one folder. He knows the letters were sent. Beat: cold menace; we meet the antagonist without naming his crime.

chapters.title: A Witness Named Nobody
chapters.summary: Isandro tracks down Dolores Kane, a retired dispatcher who worked the night in question. She's terrified, denies everything, then slips: 'Your father drove that car.' Beat: the personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: What Papa Drove
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, memory chapter. Fragmented childhood recollections: a father who came home at dawn smelling of cigarettes and fear, then vanished. Beat: grief reframed as evidence.

chapters.title: Second Letter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A second letter arrives with a ledger page photocopied inside and a deadline: decode it before the statute expires in ninety days, or 'the next confession names you.' Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Night Manager
chapters.summary: POV: Renata, current Meridian manager, pressured by Vey's lawyer to hand over archives. She resists quietly, becoming an unwitting ally. Beat: institutional rot glimpsed from inside.

chapters.title: Cipher of Fares
chapters.summary: Isandro works the code: fares encode times, routes encode addresses, driver numbers encode people. Entry one confirms the victim: a union organizer named Tomas Reyes. Beat: intellectual momentum, moral weight.

chapters.title: Dolores Breaks
chapters.summary: Dolores POV. Someone ransacks her apartment. She calls Isandro at 3 a.m., half-confessing she saw the body and was paid to forget. Beat: fear becomes testimony.

chapters.title: The Man Who Paid
chapters.summary: Isandro follows money trails: hush payments routed through a shell charity Vey still chairs. Beat: power's architecture exposed—corruption as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Ghost Driver Number Seven
chapters.summary: Ledger entry seven lists Isandro's father, Emilio, as driver on the cleanup run. Isandro realizes the letters' sender may be Emilio himself—or someone holding his effects. Beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Renata Opens the Archive
chapters.summary: Renata POV. She copies the pre-2005 dispatch tapes for Isandro, knowing it could end her career. Beat: solidarity kindles; small courage against large machinery.

chapters.title: Tape Hiss
chapters.summary: Isandro listens to degraded audio: a dispatcher's voice—Dolores—young and shaking, logging a fare to the ravine. Beat: the past speaking directly; chills.

chapters.title: Vey's Offer
chapters.summary: Vey summons Isandro through his lawyer: a job, money, silence. He speaks in warm generalities, never confessing. Beat: seduction of complicity; Isandro nearly understands how their father was bought.

chapters.title: Third Letter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The third letter contains a photograph of young Emilio with Vey, and one line: 'He wanted to tell you. I promised him you'd read it instead.' Beat: the sender's identity narrows; tenderness inside menace.

chapters.title: Who Wrote in the Margins
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis by a graphologist friend points to someone left-handed, older, trained as a dispatcher. Isandro suspects Dolores. Beat: misdirection peak.

chapters.title: Dolores Dies Quietly
chapters.summary: Dolores found dead—officially a heart attack. Isandro knows better. Beat: guilt, fury, escalation; the game turns lethal.

chapters.title: The Ravine at Noon
chapters.summary: Isandro visits the ravine where Reyes died, finds a weathered marker someone maintains yearly. Fresh flowers. Beat: mourning meets detection; the sender has been here recently.

chapters.title: Midnight Shift Stakeout
chapters.summary: Isandro waits at the ravine through a full night shift, radio crackling. At dawn, an old man leaves flowers: Mateo Reyes, the victim's brother, a retired Meridian mechanic. Beat: the sender revealed—not a threat, a mourner.

chapters.title: Mateo's Confession of Sorts
chapters.summary: Mateo POV. He sent the letters: he's dying, the statute expires soon, and he needed someone outside Vey's reach to finish decoding. He apologizes for terrorizing Isandro. Beat: relief laced with anger; alliance formed.

chapters.title: Emilio's Last Run
chapters.summary: Mateo shares what Emilio told him before vanishing: Emilio drove the body, kept a duplicate ledger page as insurance, then disappeared—possibly killed. Beat: Isandro's inheritance clarified as burden.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Isandro deduces the final ledger page—the one naming Vey explicitly—is hidden in plain sight: framed on Meridian's office wall as 'founder's memorabilia.' Beat: elegant turn; the clue was always visible.

chapters.title: Renata's Gamble
chapters.summary: Renata lets Isandro into the office after hours. Behind the frame: Emilio's page, plus a letter to 'my child.' Beat: emotional apex of the mystery thread; tears over evidence.

chapters.title: Letter From My Father
chapters.summary: Isandro reads Emilio's letter: he couldn't live with what he did, he hid the proof, he chose disappearance over betrayal either way. Beat: forgiveness begins; identity theme crystallizes.

chapters.title: Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Eleven days remain. Vey's lawyer moves to have the archive sealed; a judge sympathetic to Vey grants a temporary order. Beat: legal walls closing; despair.

chapters.title: Leak Planning
chapters.summary: Isandro, Mateo, and Renata plan publication: a journalist, a dead-man's switch, copies everywhere. Beat: resolve hardens into strategy; found-family warmth.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Waited
chapters.summary: POV: Odile Ferran, investigative reporter who chased the Reyes case twenty years ago and was ruined for it. She agrees instantly. Beat: vindication deferred finally arriving.

chapters.title: Vey Learns Everything
chapters.summary: Vey POV. His lawyer reports the breach. Vey orders a 'final cleanup,' revealing he's arranged deaths before without lifting a finger himself. Beat: villain fully unveiled; icy competence.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Isandro notices a cab following their route home—Meridian plates, no passenger. A warning. Beat: paranoia made literal; the hunter hunted.

chapters.title: Safehouse Above the Garage
chapters.summary: Isandro hides in Mateo's old garage apartment. First time relying on others in decades. Beat: vulnerability as strength; belonging tasted.

chapters.title: The Dead-Man's Switch
chapters.summary: Odile loads the story; documents distributed to three outlets. If anything happens to any of them, everything publishes. Beat: checkmate positioning; held breath.

chapters.title: Vey's Countermove
chapters.summary: Vey preemptively announces a charitable foundation in Reyes's name, laundering his legacy before the story lands. Beat: audacity of power; public relations as alibi.

chapters.title: Publication Eve
chapters.summary: Isandro can't sleep; walks the city they've hidden in, deciding whether to attach their real name to the story. Beat: the thematic crux—invisibility versus witness.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Odile's exposé runs: 'The Ledger of Meridian.' Isandro insists on being quoted under their full birth name. Beat: climax of identity; claiming the self.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Harbor House
chapters.summary: Isandro visits Vey unannounced. The old man neither denies nor apologizes; he offers Isandro a place in his world. Isandro refuses and reads Emilio's letter aloud. Beat: true climax; power met with witness.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Prosecutors reopen the case using the ledger; Vey is indicted before the statute question is even resolved—obstruction charges stick regardless. Renata keeps her job; Odile wins an award. Beat: justice, partial and real.

chapters.title: What the Grave Holds
chapters.summary: Cold-case divers find remains in the reservoir matching Emilio. Isandro buries a father they barely knew, attended by Mateo, Renata, Odile. Beat: grief completed; family chosen.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Daylight
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Isandro's POV. Isandro takes a day-shift training role at Meridian under new ownership, name badge worn openly. A new dispatcher asks about the famous ledger; Isandro smiles and begins the story. Beat: resolution—belonging earned, invisibility voluntarily ended.
